subproblems.title: Helly selection: no limiting mass concentration at levels outside a countable set
subproblems.statement: Let μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ, let a, b ∈ ℝ and let Λ ∈ [0, ∞) satisfy μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ for every j. Then there exist a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a countable set N ⊆ ℝ such that for every s ∈ (a, b) with s ∉ N and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is δ > 0 with μ_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all sufficiently large j.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (μ : ℕ → Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (Λ : ℝ≥0∞), Λ ≠ ∞ → (∀ j, μ j (Icc a b) ≤ Λ) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (N : Set ℝ), StrictMono φ ∧ N.Countable ∧ ∀ s ∈ Ioo a b, s ∉ N → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, μ (φ j) (Icc (s - δ) s) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0–3 of the parent-supplied proof of dimred_mbl_fc_good_slice, together with the case ε = ∞ of its step 8: Helly's selection argument and the countability of the discontinuity set of the monotone limit distribution function. These realize ingredient (α) of Simon, Ch. 6, proof of 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2090–2099, "by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2"): compactness of the mass-bounded measures, together with the countability of the levels that carry positive limit mass.

The parent text is adjusted in two harmless ways.
(a) The countable set D = ℚ ∩ (a, b) itself indexes the Tychonoff product. So neither an enumeration of D nor the hypothesis a < b is needed. If b ≤ a, then (a, b) = ∅ and the final claim is vacuous; the argument runs verbatim with D possibly empty.
(b) The claim is proved for the original measures μ_j with the non-strict bound ≤ ε for every ε ∈ (0, ∞]. The case ε = ∞ is trivial.

1. (Restriction.) For j ∈ ℕ let ν_j := μ_j⌞[a, b], i.e. ν_j(E) = μ_j(E ∩ [a, b]) for Borel E ⊆ ℝ. Then ν_j(ℝ) = μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ < ∞. Hence each ν_j is a finite Borel measure, ν_j(E) ≤ Λ for every Borel E, and ν_j(E) = μ_j(E) for every Borel E ⊆ [a, b].

2. (Helly selection.) Let D := {d ∈ ℚ : a < d < b}, a countable set. For j ∈ ℕ define v_j : D → ℝ by v_j(d) := ν_j([a, d]).toReal. Since 0 ≤ ν_j([a, d]) ≤ Λ < ∞ and toReal is monotone on finite values, v_j(d) ∈ [0, Λ.toReal].
So every v_j lies in K := Π_{d∈D} [0, Λ.toReal] ⊆ ℝ^D, which is compact by Tychonoff (Mathlib isCompact_univ_pi). The space ℝ^D is a countable product of metric spaces, hence first countable.
By Mathlib IsCompact.tendsto_subseq there are G ∈ K and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with v_{φ(j)} → G in ℝ^D. Convergence in the product topology is coordinatewise (Mathlib tendsto_pi_nhds), so
 (2.1) ν_{φ(j)}([a, d]).toReal → G(d) as j → ∞, for every d ∈ D.
From G ∈ K, 0 ≤ G(d) ≤ Λ.toReal for every d ∈ D.
If d, d' ∈ D and d ≤ d', then [a, d] ⊆ [a, d'], so ν_j([a, d]).toReal ≤ ν_j([a, d']).toReal for every j (both values are finite). Limits preserve non-strict inequalities, so passing to the limit in (2.1) gives G(d) ≤ G(d').

3. (Limit distribution function.) For t ∈ ℝ let A_t := {0} ∪ {G(d) : d ∈ D, d < t} and G̃(t) := sup A_t. A_t is nonempty and bounded above by Λ.toReal, so G̃(t) is a well-defined real number.
If t ≤ t', then A_t ⊆ A_{t'}, hence G̃(t) ≤ G̃(t'). So G̃ : ℝ → ℝ is nondecreasing, and therefore the set
 N := {t ∈ ℝ : G̃ is not continuous at t}
is countable (Mathlib Monotone.countable_not_continuousAt). Moreover:
 (α) if d ∈ D and d < t, then G(d) ∈ A_t, so G(d) ≤ G̃(t);
 (β) if d ∈ D and t < d, then G̃(t) ≤ G(d). Indeed every element of A_t is ≤ G(d): the element 0 satisfies 0 ≤ G(d), and an element G(d') with d' ∈ D, d' < t satisfies d' < d, hence G(d') ≤ G(d) by step 2.

4. (The claim; the case ε = ∞.) We show that φ from step 2 (strictly increasing) and N from step 3 (countable) satisfy the conclusion. Let s ∈ (a, b) with s ∉ N, so G̃ is continuous at s, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞].
If ε = ∞, then δ := 1 > 0 works, since every value of a measure is ≤ ∞.
Assume from now on that ε < ∞, and put e := ε.toReal. Then e > 0 because 0 < ε < ∞, and ENNReal.ofReal(e) = ε.

5. (Choice of δ.) By continuity of G̃ at s, choose η₀ > 0 such that |G̃(t) − G̃(s)| < e/2 whenever |t − s| < η₀. Put η := min(η₀/3, (s − a)/3, (b − s)/2). Since s − a > 0 and b − s > 0, η > 0; moreover 2η < η₀, 2η < s − a and s + η < b.
By density of ℚ in ℝ (Mathlib exists_rat_btwn), choose rationals d₁, d₂ with s − 2η < d₁ < s − η and s < d₂ < s + η. Then a < s − 2η < d₁ < s < b and a < s < d₂ < s + η < b, so d₁, d₂ ∈ D and d₁ < s < d₂.
By (β) with t = s − 2η < d₁, G̃(s − 2η) ≤ G(d₁). By (α) with d₂ < s + η = t, G(d₂) ≤ G̃(s + η).
Since |(s + η) − s| = η < η₀ and |(s − 2η) − s| = 2η < η₀, we have G̃(s + η) < G̃(s) + e/2 and G̃(s − 2η) > G̃(s) − e/2. Consequently
 (5.1) G(d₂) − G(d₁) ≤ G̃(s + η) − G̃(s − 2η) < e.
Set δ := η > 0.

6. (Mass bound for each j.) Fix j. Since a < s − 2η < s − δ and s < b, [s − δ, s] ⊆ [a, b], so μ_j([s − δ, s]) = ν_j([s − δ, s]) by step 1.
Further, [s − δ, s] ⊆ [a, d₂] ∖ [a, d₁]: a point x with s − δ ≤ x ≤ s satisfies a < x ≤ s < d₂ and x ≥ s − η > d₁.
Since d₁ < d₂, [a, d₁] ⊆ [a, d₂]. As ν_j([a, d₁]) < ∞, finite additivity (Mathlib measure_sdiff) gives
 ν_j([a, d₂] ∖ [a, d₁]) = ν_j([a, d₂]) − ν_j([a, d₁]) = ENNReal.ofReal(x_j),
where x_j := ν_j([a, d₂]).toReal − ν_j([a, d₁]).toReal is a difference of finite values (ENNReal.ofReal_sub and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). By monotonicity of ν_j,
 (6.1) μ_j([s − δ, s]) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(x_j).

7. (Eventual smallness.) By (2.1), x_{φ(j)} → G(d₂) − G(d₁) as j → ∞, and this limit is < e by (5.1). Hence x_{φ(j)} < e for all sufficiently large j.
For every such j, (6.1) and monotonicity of ENNReal.ofReal give
 μ_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(x_{φ(j)}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(e) = ε.
So δ > 0 and μ_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all sufficiently large j. Together with the case ε = ∞ of step 4, this proves the claim for every s ∈ (a, b) ∖ N and every ε ∈ (0, ∞], with φ strictly increasing and N countable. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict to [a, b]: ν_j := μ_j⌞[a, b] is a finite Borel measure with ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ that agrees with μ_j on Borel subsets of [a, b].

Tychonoff on Π_{d∈ℚ∩(a,b)} [0, Λ.toReal] (first countable, as the index set is countable) gives a strictly increasing φ and G with ν_{φ(j)}([a, d]).toReal → G(d) for every rational d ∈ (a, b). G is nondecreasing with values in [0, Λ.toReal].
G̃(t) := sup({0} ∪ {G(d) : d < t}) is nondecreasing, so its discontinuity set N is countable. Also G(d) ≤ G̃(t) for d < t, and G̃(t) ≤ G(d) for t < d.
The case ε = ∞ is trivial. Otherwise, at a continuity point s ∈ (a, b) ∖ N, choose η > 0 and rationals d₁ ∈ (s − 2η, s − η), d₂ ∈ (s, s + η) with G(d₂) − G(d₁) < ε.toReal, and put δ := η.
μ_j([s − δ, s]) ≤ ν_j([a, d₂] ∖ [a, d₁]) = ofReal(ν_j([a, d₂]).toReal − ν_j([a, d₁]).toReal). Along φ this real number tends to G(d₂) − G(d₁) < ε.toReal, so μ_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all large j.

subproblems.title: Tonelli–Fatou: lower left difference quotients have a.e. finite liminf over j
subproblems.statement: Let μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ, let a, b ∈ ℝ and let Λ ∈ [0, ∞) satisfy μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ for every j. For t ∈ ℝ and j ∈ ℕ let S_j(t) := liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j((t − h, t)) ∈ [0, ∞] (limit inferior in [0, ∞] along h → 0 with h > 0, i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0). Then for Lebesgue-almost every t ∈ ℝ: if a < t < b, then liminf_{j→∞} S_j(t) ≠ ∞ (limit inferior in [0, ∞] along atTop in ℕ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (μ : ℕ → Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (Λ : ℝ≥0∞), Λ ≠ ∞ → (∀ j, μ j (Icc a b) ≤ Λ) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun j => liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ j (Ioo (t - h) t)) (𝓝[>] 0)) atTop ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 4 of the parent-supplied proof of dimred_mbl_fc_good_slice, together with the comparison made in its step 7. These are measurable majorants of the slice quantity (lim infs of lower difference quotients), controlled by Tonelli's theorem and two applications of Fatou's lemma. They realize ingredient (β) of Simon, Ch. 6, proof of 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2090–2099): the Fatou argument for the derivatives F_j' of the monotone functions F_j, with lim infs of difference quotients in place of F_j'.

The parent text is adjusted in three ways.
(a) The statement concerns an arbitrary sequence μ_j with μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ. The parent applies it to the Helly subsequence j ↦ μ_{φ₁(j)}, which satisfies the same bound.
(b) The hypothesis a < b is not needed: if b ≤ a, the implication is vacuous.
(c) The conclusion is stated for S_j itself, because the comparison S_j(t) ≤ q_j(t) of parent step 7 is proved here (step 5).

Notation: S_j(t) := liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j((t − h, t)) ∈ [0, ∞] is the limit inferior along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. Leb denotes Lebesgue measure on ℝ, ∫⁻ the [0, ∞]-valued Lebesgue integral, and "almost every" refers to Leb.

1. (Restriction.) For j ∈ ℕ let ν_j := μ_j⌞[a, b], i.e. ν_j(E) = μ_j(E ∩ [a, b]) for Borel E. Then ν_j(ℝ) = μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ < ∞. So ν_j is a finite (in particular s-finite) Borel measure, and ν_j(E) = μ_j(E) for every Borel E ⊆ [a, b].

2. (Measurability and Tonelli.) Fix j and h ∈ ℝ, and let E_h := {(t, x) ∈ ℝ × ℝ : t − h < x and x < t}. It is the intersection of two sets of the form {f < g} with f, g continuous, hence Borel.
For fixed t, its section {x : (t, x) ∈ E_h} is the interval (t − h, t). For fixed x, its section {t : (t, x) ∈ E_h} is (x, x + h), since t − h < x < t ⟺ x < t < x + h.
Because ν_j is s-finite, t ↦ ν_j((t − h, t)) = ν_j({x : (t, x) ∈ E_h}) is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left).
Now compute the product measure Leb ⊗ ν_j of E_h by integrating sections in either order (Mathlib Measure.prod_apply and Measure.prod_apply_symm; both factors are s-finite), using Leb((x, x + h)) = ENNReal.ofReal(h) (Mathlib Real.volume_Ioo):
 ∫⁻ ν_j((t − h, t)) dt = (Leb ⊗ ν_j)(E_h) = ∫⁻ Leb((x, x + h)) dν_j(x) = ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(h) dν_j(x) = ENNReal.ofReal(h)·ν_j(ℝ).

3. (First application of Fatou.) For n ∈ ℕ put h_n := 1/(n + 1) > 0. For t ∈ ℝ put Q_{j,n}(t) := (n + 1)·ν_j((t − h_n, t)) ∈ [0, ∞], with n + 1 read in [0, ∞]. By step 2, Q_{j,n} is measurable.
In [0, ∞], ENNReal.ofReal(1/(n + 1)) = (n + 1)⁻¹ and n + 1 ∉ {0, ∞}, so (n + 1)·ENNReal.ofReal(h_n) = 1. Pulling the constant out of the integral of a measurable function (Mathlib lintegral_const_mul), step 2 gives
 ∫⁻ Q_{j,n} = (n + 1)·ENNReal.ofReal(h_n)·ν_j(ℝ) = ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ.
Let q_j(t) := liminf_{n→∞} Q_{j,n}(t). It is measurable as a sequential liminf of measurable functions (Mathlib Measurable.liminf). Fatou's lemma (Mathlib lintegral_liminf_le) gives ∫⁻ q_j ≤ liminf_n ∫⁻ Q_{j,n} = ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ.

4. (Second application of Fatou.) The function t ↦ liminf_{j→∞} q_j(t) is measurable, again by Measurable.liminf. By Fatou's lemma again, ∫⁻ liminf_j q_j ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻ q_j ≤ Λ < ∞; the last liminf is ≤ Λ because each of its terms is ≤ Λ by step 3.
A measurable [0, ∞]-valued function with finite integral is finite almost everywhere (Mathlib ae_lt_top). Hence there is a Lebesgue-null set Z such that liminf_j q_j(t) < ∞ for every t ∉ Z.

5. (Comparison S_j ≤ q_j on (a, b).) Fix t with a < t < b and fix j ∈ ℕ. The sequence h_n = 1/(n + 1) tends to 0 (Mathlib tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat) through positive values, i.e. h_n → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (Mathlib tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff).
For any u : ℝ → [0, ∞], the liminf of u along 𝓝[>] 0 is at most the liminf of the sequence u(h_n) (Mathlib Filter.Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp; no boundedness side conditions arise in the complete lattice [0, ∞]). With u(h) := ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j((t − h, t)) this gives
 S_j(t) ≤ liminf_n ENNReal.ofReal(h_n⁻¹)·μ_j((t − h_n, t)).
Since t − a > 0 and h_n → 0, we have h_n ≤ t − a for all sufficiently large n. For such n, (t − h_n, t) ⊆ [a, b] because t − h_n ≥ a and t < b, so μ_j((t − h_n, t)) = ν_j((t − h_n, t)) by step 1. Also ENNReal.ofReal(h_n⁻¹) = ENNReal.ofReal(n + 1) = n + 1.
So the sequence on the right agrees with Q_{j,n}(t) for all sufficiently large n. A liminf along atTop depends only on eventual values (Mathlib Filter.liminf_congr), so its liminf equals q_j(t). Hence S_j(t) ≤ q_j(t).

6. (Conclusion.) Let t ∉ Z and suppose a < t < b. By step 5, S_j(t) ≤ q_j(t) for every j. By monotonicity of liminf (Mathlib Filter.liminf_le_liminf), liminf_j S_j(t) ≤ liminf_j q_j(t), which is < ∞ by step 4; that is, liminf_j S_j(t) ≠ ∞. Since Z is Lebesgue-null, this holds for Lebesgue-almost every t, which is the statement. ∎

Tonelli on the Borel set E_h = {(t, x) : t − h < x < t}, whose sections are (t − h, t) and (x, x + h): t ↦ ν_j((t − h, t)) is measurable and ∫⁻ ν_j((t − h, t)) dt = ofReal(h)·ν_j(ℝ).
Q_{j,n}(t) := (n + 1)·ν_j((t − 1/(n + 1), t)) is measurable with ∫⁻ Q_{j,n} = ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ. By Fatou, q_j := liminf_n Q_{j,n} is measurable with ∫⁻ q_j ≤ Λ.
By Fatou again, ∫⁻ liminf_j q_j ≤ Λ < ∞, so liminf_j q_j(t) < ∞ off a Lebesgue-null set Z (ae_lt_top).

For t ∈ (a, b), h_n = 1/(n + 1) → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0 and eventually (t − h_n, t) ⊆ [a, b], so S_j(t) ≤ q_j(t) (Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp, liminf_congr). Hence liminf_j S_j(t) ≤ liminf_j q_j(t) < ∞ for t ∉ Z.
